Paragraph: "Though named 'Asoka'—the remover of sorrow—these red blossoms only deepen the sorrow in my heart..."
Situation/Problem_Faced: Irony of the 'Asoka' (sorrow-remover) tree causing more emotional sorrow.
Key_Teaching/Action_Taken: Rama reflects on the linguistic and physical irony of the Asoka tree.
Outcome/Resolution: He highlights how emotional state can invert the meaning of external symbols.

Spiritual_Psychological_Concept_Indian.Concept: Viparita-Bhavana (Inverted psychological perception where healing symbols evoke grief)

Brief_Summary_Spiritual: Shows how without inner readiness, even sorrow-removing agents (Asoka) cannot cure the ache of separation.
Brief_Summary_Psychological: Cognitive inversion: finding that symbols meant to relieve distress exacerbate pain due to unresolved grief.
